summary: During the stay at Hudaybiyyah, Umar suggests and Rasulullaah ﷺ sends Uthmaan to Makkah with a message of peace; Uthmaan gives the Quraysh da'wah and is guaranteed safe passage.

people.name: Abaan bin Sa'eed bin Al Aas

notes: Ends with 'The Hadith still continues further'; the report carries on in the next narration.

summary: Umar says Rasulullaah ﷺ made concessions in the treaty of Hudaybiyyah and that he would have obeyed any Ameer who acted as the Prophet did.

Abu Bakr says Hudaybiyyah was the greatest victory in Islaam, and recounts how Suhayl bin Amr, who had refused the title Rasool at the treaty, later honoured the Prophet at the Farewell Hajj and was guided to Islaam.
Amr bin Al Aas plots against the Prophet's envoys, then goes to Najaashi and accepts Islaam; he travels with Khaalid bin Waleed and Uthmaan bin Talha to Madinah and pledges allegiance to the Prophet.
notes: Contains the main account of Amr's conversion and a separate, more detailed Bayhaqi report from Waaqidi appended with '(l)'.

summary: Khaalid bin Waleed recounts how he came to Islaam after the treaty of Hudaybiyyah, after reading his brother Waleed's letter, dreaming, and meeting Safwaan, Ikrama, Uthmaan bin Talha and Amr bin Al Aas on the way to Madinah, where the Prophet prayed for his forgiveness.
notes: Includes an editorial footnote on Salaatul Khawf (marked '(l)') that is not part of the narration.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ left Madinah for Makkah on the tenth of Ramadhaan with ten thousand Sahabah, appointing Abu Ruhm Kulthoom as Ameer of Madinah, and camped at Marruz Zahraan.

people.name: Abu Ruhm Kulthoom bin Husayn Ghifaari

summary: Abu Sufyaan, Hakeem bin Hizaam and Budayl set out to spy on the Muslims; Abu Sufyaan bin Haarith and Abdullaah bin Abi Umayyah, the Prophet's cousins, are admitted after Umm Salma interceded and both accept Islaam.

people.name: Abu Sufyaan bin Haarith bin Abdil Muttalib

summary: Abbaas tells the Quraysh that they are doomed unless they seek amnesty before the Muslims enter Makkah by force, and rides the Prophet's white mule out to find someone to warn them.
Abbaas meets Abu Sufyaan by night and brings him to the Prophet on the mule; Umar protests, and the Prophet grants Abu Sufyaan safe passage through Abbaas.
notes: Continues Abbaas's account from the end of the previous narration (on the road to Makkah).

summary: Abu Sufyaan testifies to Tawheed and then to the Prophet's Risaalah after Abbaas urges him to accept Islaam before he is executed.

Abbaas asks for honour to be given to Abu Sufyaan, the Prophet grants safety to whoever enters Abu Sufyaan's house, locks his door or enters the Masjid, and Abu Sufyaan warns Makkah as the tribes pass by.

As the Muslims enter Makkah, Abu Sufyaan watches the tribal battalions pass with Abbaas, including those led by Khaalid, Zubayr, Abu Dharr and Sa'd bin Ubaadah, and the Prophet has Sa'd's flag handed to his son Qais.
notes: Opens with an isnaad-only reference to a report already given (Ibn Asaakir from Waaqidi), then the long account of the battalions passing. Waaqidi himself is cited and left out of people.

summary: Abu Layla reports that Abu Sufyaan was captured by the Sahabah at Araak and brought to the Prophet, who offers him Islaam and safety, and Abu Sufyaan remarks on the greatness of the Prophet's kingdom as the Ansaar pass by.

Urwa reports that Abu Sufyaan and Hakeem bin Hizaam were captured on their way to the Prophet, that Abbaas protected Abu Sufyaan, who accepted Islaam, and that the Prophet sent Abbaas to announce amnesty for Makkah while Hind attacked her husband.
notes: Ends mid-speech with Hind's words ('Go home'), and the text carries OCR debris including a Haythami footnote fragment inside the sentence.

summary: Suhayl bin Amr locks his house at the conquest, his son secures amnesty for him, the Prophet ﷺ praises him, and Suhayl later accepts Islaam at Ji'irraanah and is given a hundred camels.

Umar reports that the Prophet ﷺ, after the conquest, compared his own treatment of the Quraysh with Yusuf and his brothers and pardoned Safwaan, Abu Sufyaan and Haarith, and Umar was embarrassed at his own eagerness for revenge.
Ibn Abi Husayn and Abu Hurayrah report the Prophet ﷺ at the door of the Kabah pardoning the Quraysh with Yusuf's words, after which the people accept Islaam, and a version from Bayhaqi is added.
notes: Contains two separate reports (Ibn Abi Husayn, then Abu Hurayrah) and a Bayhaqi citation; the scholars cited in the reference line (Bayhaqi, Shafi'ee, Abu Yusuf) are left out of people.

summary: Ummu Hakeem accepts Islaam on the day of the conquest and secures amnesty for her husband Ikrama, who had fled to Yemen; she follows him to bring him back, and Ikrama kills the Roman slave who had tried to seduce her.
notes: Ikrama is described as not yet Muslim at the end of this narration.

summary: Ikrama comes to the Prophet ﷺ as a Muhaajir, is granted amnesty and wife, and accepts Islaam by testifying to the kalimah after the Prophet ﷺ tells the Sahabah not to curse his dead father.
notes: OCR debris in the Arabic kalimah text is ignored.

summary: Ikrama asks the Prophet ﷺ to pray for forgiveness for his past enmity and vows to spend double and fight double in the path of Allaah, while Suhayl bin Amr mocks his past opposition at Hunayn.
notes: Ends with a Waaqidi report about the Battle of Hunayn appended as a separate account.

summary: Abdullaah bin Zubayr and Urwa bin Zubayr each give a shorter account of Ikrama's acceptance of Islaam, the Prophet's du'aa for his forgiveness, and Ikrama's vow to spend and fight double in the path of Allaah.
notes: Two separate reports of the same meeting: Abdullaah bin Zubayr, then Urwa bin Zubayr quoting Ikrama.

summary: Ikrama is martyred in the Battle of Ajnaadeen during Abu Bakr's caliphate, having been appointed by the Prophet ﷺ to collect the zakaah of Hawaazin in the year of the farewell Hajj.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence at 'in Tabaalah (in'.

summary: Safwaan bin Umayyah flees Makkah; his wife Baghoom accepts Islaam, and Umayr bin Wahab goes to Safwaan to tell him that the Prophet ﷺ has granted him amnesty.
notes: The opening word 'Wahab' is an OCR split of the heading's name, ignored.

summary: Safwaan asks for a sign of the amnesty, Umayr brings the Prophet's turban, and after the Prophet grants him a four-month grace period Safwaan returns and dismounts to meet him.
Safwaan lends a hundred coats of armour for the Battle of Hunayn, and when the Prophet ﷺ gives him a valley of camels and shepherds at Ji'irraanah, Safwaan accepts Islaam on the spot.
Another narration of Safwaan's loan of armour: some of the coats are destroyed, the Prophet offers to pay for the damage, and Safwaan declines compensation because he wants to accept Islaam.
notes: A second version of the armour-loan report from n00145, not a merged report.

summary: Mundhir bin Jahm reports that Huwaytib, terrified after the conquest, is persuaded by Abu Dharr to come to the Prophet ﷺ and accepts Islaam, and the Prophet ﷺ then grants him a loan and a share of the Hunayn booty.

people.name: Ja'far bin Mahmood bin Muhammad bin Salma

notes: Contains Mundhir bin Jahm's report and a second report from Huwaytib via Ja'far bin Mahmood bin Muhammad bin Salma.

summary: Abdullaah bin Ikrama reports that Ummu Haani granted protection to Haarith bin Hishaam and Abdullaah bin Abi Rabee'ah, that Ali tried to attack them and was stopped, that the Prophet ﷺ upheld her protection, and that Haarith then accepted Islaam.
notes: Contains Abdullaah bin Ikrama's report and a separate report in which Ummu Haani narrates her own account to the Prophet ﷺ.

summary: Nudhayr bin Haarith, one of the most learned of the Quraysh, is made steadfast by the Prophet's du'aa, accepts Islaam, and then receives a gift of a hundred camels from the Prophet ﷺ which he shares with a man of the Banu Duwal.
notes: Ends with a section heading ('The Banu Thaqeef tribe of Taa'if Accept Islaam'); the next narration starts a new account.

summary: Urwa bin Mas'ood follows the Prophet ﷺ after he leaves Thaqeef, accepts Islaam, and asks to go back to his people, despite the Prophet warning that they would kill him.
Urwa bin Mas'ood invites his people to Islaam from his house balcony, is struck by arrows and martyred, and the Prophet ﷺ compares his example among his people to the man in Surah Yaaseen.

The Thaqeef send a delegation to the Prophet ﷺ, Mughiera bin Shu'ba meets them, and their conditions are negotiated, including the Prophet refusing to exempt them from salaah, while Abu Sufyaan and Mughiera are sent to destroy their idol.
notes: Two accounts: an unnamed-source report of the delegation's arrival and negotiations, then Uthmaan bin Abil Aas's report of their conditions.

summary: Wahab asks Jaabir about the Thaqeef's conditions, and Jaabir says the Prophet ﷺ accepted them while predicting that they would later pay zakaah and wage jihaad without being told.
notes: 'Thaqeef' is a tribe, not a named person; left in people only as the subject of the conditions. Consider dropping on review.

summary: Aws bin Hudhayfa, who came with the Banu Maalik delegates, describes the Prophet ﷺ addressing them standing each night after Isha, and explains once that he came late because he had not finished his daily Qur'aan recitation.

Ibn Ishaaq reports that Abu Bakr gave da'wah to the people who confided in him, and that Zubayr, Uthmaan, Talha, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas and Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf accepted Islaam through him and then met the Prophet ﷺ.
Asbaq, a Christian slave of Umar, is invited to Islaam and is freed on Umar's deathbed; Aslam reports Umar inviting an old Christian woman to Islaam after making wudhu with her water.
notes: Two separate reports: Asbaq's account of Umar's dealings with him, then Aslam's account of the water and the old woman.

summary: As'ad bin Zuraarah brings Mus'ab bin Umayr to the Banu Abdil Ash'hal, Usayd bin Hudhayr is sent to confront them, and Usayd listens, accepts Islaam and sends Sa'd bin Mu'aadh to them.

people.name: Abdullaah bin Abi Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm

summary: Mus'ab gives da'wah to Sa'd bin Mu'aadh, who first reproaches As'ad, then listens to the Qur'aan recited by Mus'ab, and accepts Islaam after bathing, cleansing his clothes and praying two rakaahs.
notes: Continues directly from n00157 (Usayd's report to Sa'd).

summary: Sa'd bin Mu'aadh tells the Banu Abdil Ash'hal that he will not speak to them until they believe, and the whole clan accepts Islaam by evening, after which Mus'ab continues his da'wah among the Ansaar.
notes: Refers to a report in another chapter and cites Tabraani, Abu Nu'aym and Urwa (RA) as sources; the cited sources are left out of people.

summary: Tulayb bin Umayr accepts Islaam in the house of Arqam and persuades his mother Arwa bint Abdil Muttalib, who testifies to the kalimah and keeps encouraging him to support the Prophet ﷺ.
notes: Two reports: Muhammad bin Ibraheem bin Haarith, then Abu Salma bin Abdir Rahmaan, whose report is abbreviated as 'the same as above'.
